hero.headline: Trump intelligence pick triggers Senate rebellion, threatens surveillance powers
hero.body:
President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence has ignited significant backlash from Senate Republicans and created a crisis over the renewal of critical surveillance authorities expiring next week.

Pulte, who currently heads the Federal Housing Finance Agency and is a major Republican donor from a home construction fortune, has no intelligence experience. His selection came days after Tulsi Gabbard left the role. Senior Democrats immediately warned that the appointment could derail a fragile bipartisan agreement to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which permits U.S. intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets operating outside the country without a warrant.

The standoff carries unusual leverage. Republicans need at least eight Democratic votes in the Senate to prevent Section 702 from expiring on June 12. Democratic leaders have made clear that a bipartisan deal could collapse unless Trump reverses the appointment.

Senator Mark Warner, vice-chair of the Senate intelligence committee, criticized Pulte's lack of qualifications. "What qualifications does Mr Pulte bring to the office? He has shown that he is willing to do anything that President Trump wants, legal or otherwise," Warner said during a hearing. In an NPR interview, Warner stated the appointment had upended renewal efforts. "I do not have the confidence I had yesterday," he said, warning that Pulte has "no intelligence background" and "a record of misusing private information."

Senate Majority Leader John Thune offered a notably cool response to his own president's pick, telling reporters that "we don't need a weaponized" national intelligence director and warning that Pulte would face "a lengthy road ahead" if nominated permanently. Thune privately asked Mark Warner whether Democrats could reverse course on the surveillance renewal if Pulte remained in the role.

Former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, who was the only Republican voting against Tulsi Gabbard's confirmation, said on Wednesday that anyone in this role "must have the extensive national security experience required by statute, and no nominee who falls short of this requirement will earn my vote."

Senior Trump administration officials struggled to defend the appointment publicly. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent did not endorse the decision during congressional hearings.

Critics worry Pulte could weaponize the intelligence community against political opponents. He has previously leveled unproven fraud allegations at Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook while at the FHFA, allegations Trump tried to use to remove her from the Fed's board. Cook has denied wrongdoing, and the matter is now before the Supreme Court.

The current Section 702 renewal bill, circulated by Senators Tom Cotton and Chuck Grassley, would extend the program through June 2029 and include new penalties for intelligence abuses and additional FBI search requirements.

cards.headline: U.S. House Votes to Halt Iran War
cards.teaser: The House delivered a rebuke to President Trump by voting 215-208 to pass a measure aimed at halting war with Iran, though the measure is largely symbolic.
cards.body:
The U.S. House of Representatives voted 215-208 to pass a war powers resolution aimed at limiting military action against Iran. Four Republicans—Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan—joined Democrats in supporting the measure, delivering a rebuke to President Trump.

The resolution would require the president to seek congressional approval before continuing military operations against Iran or withdraw U.S. forces from the region. Though largely symbolic and lacking binding legal force, the vote demonstrates significant congressional concern about potential escalation in the ongoing tensions between the two countries.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon Agree to Renew Cease-Fire
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a renewed cease-fire arrangement brokered by the United States. The Trump administration announced the agreement following negotiations in Washington, with the deal requiring a complete cessation of fire from Hezbollah, an Iran-aligned armed group operating in southern Lebanon.

Under the terms of the agreement, Hezbollah must stop all attacks and evacuate its fighters from the area south of the Litani River in southern Lebanon. Both countries have rejected "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage," according to a joint statement released by the U.S. State Department.

While the agreement was signed between the governments of Lebanon and Israel, the actual fighting has been between Hezbollah and Israel. The Lebanese army has not been a direct party to the conflict. However, the Lebanese government has been negotiating with Israel in an effort to reassert government control over the country and disarm the armed group.

The two countries also agreed to create "pilot zones" in which the Lebanese armed forces will take exclusive control of territory to the exclusion of all non-state actors. The joint statement indicated that ongoing meetings in Washington would continue to flesh out the cease-fire details and plan its phased implementation.

However, the agreement faces immediate credibility questions. Despite the announced accord, Israel carried out multiple drone strikes in southern Lebanon on Thursday morning, raising doubts about commitment to the arrangement. Additionally, a previous cease-fire scheduled to take hold on April 17 failed, with both sides continuing hostilities and accusing each other of violations.

A Hezbollah official told media outlets that the group would not accept a partial cease-fire and had not been party to the talks. The group signaled privately, however, that it is ready for a complete cease-fire, meaning it would refrain from attacks if Israel also stopped strikes. Hezbollah has stated it will not return to the pre-war status quo, under which Israel conducted frequent strikes despite the existence of a previous cease-fire.

The cease-fire agreement resembles a 2024 arrangement in which Hezbollah agreed to pull back from south of the Litani River so Lebanese armed forces could deploy there. That earlier accord failed to achieve Hezbollah's full disarmament, and Israel carried out more than 10,000 strikes in violation of the cease-fire during the 15 months that followed.

The negotiations come as the U.S. seeks to resolve broader regional conflicts, including the war with Iran. President Trump has indicated he wants to separate talks on the Lebanon conflict from negotiations with Iran, though Tehran insists the conflicts are linked. The fate of Hezbollah is understood to be connected to outcomes of negotiations with Iran and potentially a broader political settlement in the region.

cards.headline: Netanyahu tensions with Trump grow over Lebanon military strategy
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces competing pressures from Trump and domestic politics as their military objectives diverge.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's recent disagreement with President Trump over Lebanon strategy has strained their typically close relationship. Trump confirmed he called Netanyahu "crazy" during a heated phone call in which he told the Israeli leader not to bomb Beirut.

Despite their frequent coordination on Iran policy and near-daily conversations, the two leaders have shown diverging priorities. Netanyahu faces pressure from domestic politics while Trump has demonstrated less enthusiasm for military escalation in the region, creating tension in what has otherwise been a closely coordinated partnership on Middle East policy.

cards.headline: SpaceX targets $1.75 trillion valuation in largest IPO ever planned
cards.body:
SpaceX plans to raise approximately $75 billion through what would become the largest initial public offering in history. The space exploration company has set a target share price of $135 per share, which would value the company at $1.77 trillion.

The offering would be a historic moment for founder Elon Musk, potentially positioning him to become the world's first trillionaire. According to Forbes, Musk's current net worth stands at $825 billion, with his SpaceX stake valued at $542 billion. Musk is not selling any of his shares in the IPO and would retain 82.4% of the company's voting power.

The company, formally known as Space Exploration Technologies Corp, made the announcement through a securities filing on Wednesday. The roadshow to pitch the company to investors was expected to begin shortly after the filing. JP Morgan Chase boss Jamie Dimon reportedly planned to host a discussion about the IPO for thousands of high net worth clients, joined by SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and chief financial officer Bret Johnsen.

Goldman Sachs was selected as the lead underwriter for the offering, alongside Morgan Stanley. Twenty-three banks total are working on the listing, including JP Morgan, Bank of America, and Citigroup.

The IPO would have a significant impact on the broader stock market. Given SpaceX's enormous valuation, it would have substantial weighting in the S&P 500 index, meaning most people with investment accounts or pension funds would be exposed to the company's stock performance. Only six companies in the blue chip index are currently worth more than SpaceX, with semiconductor company Nvidia topping the list at $5.2 trillion.

SpaceX has built a dominant position in commercial spaceflight since its founding in 2002. The company holds major contracts with NASA and the Department of Defense and operates the Starlink satellite internet service, which provides connectivity worldwide. The reusable Falcon 9 rocket has become the workhorse of the commercial launch industry.

The company is also expanding into artificial intelligence, having acquired Musk's xAI to build solar-powered infrastructure supporting AI technology. This move places SpaceX among competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI in the race to scale AI capabilities. The flurry of recent IPOs and fundraising across the tech sector has been widely interpreted as an effort to generate capital for data centers powering AI technology.

The offering comes as the company continues development of its Starship vehicle, designed for missions to the Moon and Mars. The public capital would support these ambitious future projects while providing liquidity for early investors and employees holding stock options.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm found in US cattle for first time since 1960s
cards.teaser: The Agriculture Department confirmed a case of New World screwworm in a calf in South Texas, marking the pest's first detection in the country in decades.
cards.body:
A flesh-eating parasite that was eliminated from the United States in the 1960s has been detected in American cattle. The Agriculture Department confirmed that a calf in South Texas tested positive for New World screwworm, a pest that infests wounds on warm-blooded animals and feeds on living tissue.

The screwworm was eradicated from the United States through a sustained campaign that released sterile male flies to disrupt breeding cycles. The detection raises concerns about how the pest returned and whether it has established a foothold that could threaten livestock across the region.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm infection detected in South Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed a case of flesh-eating screwworm in South Texas, marking the parasite's first breach of the U.S.-Mexico border.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a case of screwworm infection in South Texas, representing the first time the flesh-eating parasite has crossed the U.S.-Mexico border. The detection raises concerns about the spread of the invasive fly species, which lays eggs in open wounds on animals and humans.

Screwworm larvae feed on living tissue, creating serious health risks for livestock and potentially humans. The confirmation of this case marks a significant development in pest control efforts along the southern border, where officials have worked to prevent the northward spread of the parasite. The USDA has previously maintained eradication programs to keep screwworm out of the United States.

cards.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
cards.teaser: The Iranian-French author and illustrator died at age 56, leaving behind a graphic novel series that humanized Iranians for millions of readers worldwide.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, author of the acclaimed graphic novel series Persepolis, has died at age 56. Her work, published in English in 2003, followed an Iranian girl through the Islamic revolution and the Iran-Iraq War.

The graphic novel series humanized Iranians for millions of readers around the world, offering a personal perspective on life during and after the 1979 revolution. Satrapi's autobiographical work became widely studied in schools and universities and was later adapted into an animated film.

cards.headline: U.S. House Votes to Halt Iran War
cards.teaser: The House delivered a rebuke to President Trump by voting 215-208 to pass a measure aimed at halting war with Iran, though the measure is largely symbolic.

The U.S. House of Representatives voted 215-208 to pass a war powers resolution aimed at limiting military action against Iran. cards.headline: Ukraine Accused of Killing Four in Occupied Crimea
cards.teaser: Russian-backed officials in Crimea reported that Ukrainian attacks killed at least four people and injured ten others in the occupied territory.
cards.body:
At least four people were killed and ten injured in attacks in occupied Crimea, according to Russian-backed officials. The officials accused Ukraine of carrying out the attacks.

Crimea has been under Russian occupation since 2014, when Russia annexed the peninsula from Ukraine. The territory remains a flashpoint in the ongoing conflict between the two countries, with Ukraine maintaining that Crimea is Ukrainian territory under illegal occupation.

cards.headline: Heavy Gunfire in Somalia's Capital as Election Dispute Escalates
cards.teaser: Heavy gunfire broke out in Mogadishu after the opposition called for protests over the president's decision to extend his term by one year.
cards.body:
Heavy gunfire erupted in Somalia's capital Mogadishu as tensions escalated over election delays. The opposition called for protests after the president extended his term in office by one year.

The extension triggered a political crisis, with opposition groups rejecting the move as unconstitutional. The violence reflects deepening tensions over the delayed electoral process and disputes about the legitimacy of the president's continued rule.

cards.headline: South Korea's Democratic Party Sweeps Local Elections but Loses Seoul Mayor's Race
cards.teaser: President Lee Jae Myung's Democratic Party won local elections across South Korea but suffered a setback in the race for Seoul mayor.
cards.body:
South Korea's governing Democratic Party swept local elections across the country but faced a setback in the Seoul mayoral race. President Lee Jae Myung's party had hoped to consolidate its influence and extend his political momentum.

The loss of the Seoul mayoral position represents a significant blow to the party despite its broader success in local elections. Seoul, as the capital and largest city, carries substantial political weight in South Korean politics.

cards.headline: China Bans Four New Zealand Lawmakers Over Taiwan Visit
cards.teaser: China imposed a one-year ban on four New Zealand members of parliament following their visit to Taiwan last month.
cards.body:
China has banned four New Zealand lawmakers for one year following their visit to Taiwan last month. The parliamentarians were notified of the ban when they returned home.

The sanctions underscore China's stance against foreign government interactions with Taiwan, which Beijing considers part of its territory. New Zealand, along with most countries, does not officially recognize Taiwan as independent but maintains informal ties with the island.

hero.headline: National Guard deployment shows no impact on violent crime in Washington, D.C.
hero.body:
A new study has found that the National Guard's presence in Washington, D.C. has had no measurable effect on violent crime in the city. Despite this finding, the federal government is moving forward with plans to expand the deployment significantly.

Nearly 2,400 National Guard troops are currently stationed in the capital, according to CNN, at a cost of approximately $1 million per day. The troops were originally set to leave at the end of November, but the deployment has been extended through at least February by Pete Hegseth, who leads the U.S. Department of Defense.

The Guard has been operating in Washington since last August as part of a federal task force aimed at reducing crime. The decision to continue and expand their presence comes despite research showing their deployment has not reduced violent crime rates.

The continued military presence in the nation's capital has become increasingly controversial. Brian Schwalb, the District of Columbia's attorney general, has characterized the deployment as an "involuntary military occupation" and has sued the Trump administration, arguing it represents an illegal use of military forces for domestic law enforcement.

The Washington deployment is part of a broader federal strategy to address crime in major cities. Following the initial dispatch to Washington, the administration has sent National Guard troops to Chicago and has threatened deployments to other Democratic-led cities including San Francisco, Portland, and New York.

Legal challenges to these deployments have already emerged. A federal judge in California ruled in September that Trump's deployment of National Guard troops to Los Angeles following protests was illegal. However, that ruling does not directly apply to Washington, where the president has greater authority over the National Guard compared to deployments in states.

The expansion of the Guard's role extends beyond Washington. The Pentagon has ordered National Guard units in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories to form "quick reaction forces" trained in riot control tactics. These forces are being trained to use batons, body shields, Tasers, and pepper spray, according to an internal Pentagon directive.

Most states are required to train at least 500 National Guard members for these quick reaction forces, bringing the total to approximately 23,500 troops nationwide. State guard units are required to report monthly on their progress in developing these capabilities.

The decision to maintain and expand the Guard's presence in Washington despite the study's findings demonstrating no crime reduction represents a significant federal intervention in urban policing. The deployment marks one of the more extensive domestic uses of military personnel for law enforcement purposes in recent memory and has drawn sharp criticism from Democratic officials and local organizers across affected cities.

cards.headline: Aircraft carrier returns home for sewage system repairs
cards.teaser: USS Gerald R. Ford and its 4,600 sailors have returned to port for repairs to the ship's sewage system.
cards.body:
The USS Gerald R. Ford has returned home after deployment with 4,600 sailors aboard. The $13 billion aircraft carrier will now undergo repairs and upgrades while docked.

The ship's sewage system will receive significant attention during the maintenance period, addressing problems that have plagued the vessel. Additional repairs and upgrades are also planned during this docking phase.

cards.headline: Students with disabilities worry about screen bans affecting assistive technology
cards.teaser: As schools move to limit screen time, students who rely on assistive technology express concern about losing access to learning tools.
cards.body:
Some students with disabilities rely on screens at school to access assistive technology that enables them to learn. As schools move to remove devices from classrooms, these students and their families worry their essential tools could get caught up in the effort.

The push to eliminate screens from schools has grown as educators work to reduce digital distractions. But for students who depend on technology for accessibility, these devices serve a critical educational purpose rather than functioning as recreational or general learning screens.

cards.headline: Cell carriers deploy drones and mobile equipment for hurricane season
cards.teaser: Phone companies are preparing networks for hurricane season with new technology, despite forecasts of milder storm activity.
cards.body:
Cell phone companies are preparing extensively for hurricane season with advanced technology, including artificial intelligence, drones, and mobile equipment. Despite forecasts predicting a milder hurricane season than usual, carriers are maintaining their full readiness efforts.

The preparations are designed to keep network coverage operational during and after storms hit coastal areas. These tools help ensure communication systems remain functional when hurricanes threaten communities.

cards.headline: World Cup heat analysis shows more than one third of matches face dangerous conditions
cards.teaser: An analysis of 2026 World Cup venues found that over a third of matches could take place in dangerously hot and humid weather.
cards.body:
An NPR analysis of weather data reveals that more than one in three matches at the 2026 World Cup will be played under dangerous heat conditions. The tournament will take place across multiple North American venues where dangerously hot and humid weather is likely during scheduled matches.

These heat conditions pose significant risks to both players and spectators attending the games. The analysis examined historical weather patterns at the host cities to identify which matches face the greatest heat-related dangers.

cards.headline: Obama Presidential Center set to open in Chicago
cards.teaser: The Obama Presidential Center will open later this month in Chicago, with preview images now available.
cards.body:
The Obama Presidential Center is scheduled to open later this month in Chicago. Preview photographs offer a look inside the facility before its public opening.

The center will join other presidential libraries and museums across the country. The Chicago location holds significance as the city where Barack Obama began his political career and maintained his home.

cards.headline: Just 3 percent of U.S. households pay for personal AI services
cards.teaser: A small fraction of American households currently subscribe to paid AI services, though sign-ups are growing.
cards.body:
Only 3 percent of U.S. households currently pay for artificial intelligence services for personal use. This low adoption rate reflects broader consumer resistance to subscription services, as Americans report experiencing subscription fatigue.

However, the picture is evolving. Sign-ups for paid AI services are growing despite the current low penetration. As AI technology continues to develop, the industry faces a key question: whether these services will remain primarily free offerings or transition toward subscription-based business models.

cards.headline: Stock futures decline as Middle East tensions end nine-day winning streak
cards.teaser: S&P 500 futures fell after the index closed lower, breaking a nine-day advance as investors reacted to escalating conflict involving Iran.
cards.body:
Stock index futures fell in early trading after the S&P 500 snapped a nine-day winning streak, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping over 600 points. Oil prices maintained gains from the previous two days.

The market decline occurred as the Trump administration announced a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon. The deal requires Hezbollah to cease fire completely and evacuate fighters from south of the Litani River. Despite the agreement, Israel conducted multiple drone strikes in southern Lebanon on Thursday morning, signaling continued military operations in the region.

cards.headline: Bitcoin falls to four-month low as crypto selloff continues
cards.teaser: Bitcoin dropped to around $61,300, marking a 13 percent decline over three days and the lowest price since before the Iran conflict began.
cards.body:
Bitcoin extended its slide, falling to its lowest level in four months as the broader cryptocurrency market continued to lose value. The token traded near $61,300 after dropping 13 percent over a three-day period.

A key market indicator signaled oversold conditions, suggesting the selloff may be approaching exhaustion. Bitcoin had rallied earlier in the year but has given back those gains as geopolitical uncertainty and risk-off sentiment have driven investors away from speculative assets.

cards.headline: US-Qatar gas dominance left global markets vulnerable to supply disruptions
cards.teaser: Before the current conflict, two countries controlled much of the liquefied natural gas market, with one now facing major operational challenges.
cards.body:
The global liquefied natural gas market had become increasingly concentrated in the hands of the United States and Qatar before recent events disrupted supply chains. The two nations commanded a growing share of LNG exports as demand for the fuel grew worldwide, particularly in Europe and Asia.

One of those two suppliers has now been hobbled, according to analysis of the market structure. The concentration of supply in so few hands has left importing nations exposed to price volatility and potential shortages when geopolitical events affect production or shipping routes.

cards.headline: Small business owners deploy AI agents to handle operations
cards.teaser: Entrepreneurs are turning artificial intelligence agents loose on core business functions including finances, email, and customer interactions.
cards.body:
Small business owners are increasingly using AI agents to automate significant portions of their operations. The technology now handles tasks ranging from financial management to customer communications, with some owners describing it as managing whole armies of AI employees.

The rapid adoption comes with risks that owners are still learning to navigate. When AI systems are given access to sensitive business functions like financial accounts and customer data, the potential for errors or unintended actions grows substantially.

cards.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT advertising campaign focused on emotional appeal
cards.teaser: A new marketing campaign for ChatGPT uses retro aesthetic and heartwarming themes to promote AI technology that polls show concerns most Americans.
cards.body:
OpenAI released an advertising campaign for ChatGPT that relies on nostalgic visuals and emotional storytelling to connect with consumers. The approach represents a shift in how the company presents its artificial intelligence product to the public.

The campaign comes as surveys show most Americans remain concerned about AI technology and its implications. The retro-themed ads appear designed to make the product feel familiar and comforting rather than highlighting technical capabilities or cutting-edge features.

hero.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch AI-powered laptops with local processing
hero.body:
Nvidia has unveiled the RTX Spark chip, a new "superchip" designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities directly to laptops and desktop computers. The move marks a significant expansion for the semiconductor company beyond its dominant position in data center hardware, pitching it against established PC chipmakers including Intel, Apple, Qualcomm and AMD.

The RTX Spark, which combines a microprocessor and graphics chip developed with Taiwan's MediaTek, is scheduled to launch this year. Computer makers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus and HP plan to use the chip paired with Microsoft's Windows software. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the partnership at Computex in Taiwan, describing the chip as a way to "reinvent the PC" for the AI era after three years of collaboration with Microsoft.

The chip is designed to run AI agents locally on personal computers rather than relying on cloud computing. This approach would allow AI agents to navigate computers autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions. Despite its power, the company stated that computers using the chip can remain thin and light.

Huang framed the development as a reimagining of the PC for the first time in 40 years. The move opens a new business line for Nvidia, though analysts cautioned that building presence in the consumer PC industry will require time to develop.

Nvidia is also introducing the Vera CPU, designed for AI agents. Early adopters of the Vera platform include OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX. These products demonstrate the company's growing focus on expanding beyond graphics cards into integrated chips that power entire computers.

Industry observers view the RTX Spark as potentially transformative. Neil Shah, co-founder of Counterpoint Research, compared the moment to the iPhone, ChatGPT and DeepSeek launches, predicting that AI-powered personal computers will eventually become commonplace. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, called it a bold attempt to extend Nvidia's dominance into consumers' daily lives, though she noted investors likely see it as a longer-term growth opportunity rather than an immediate earnings driver.

The company's pivot to personal AI computing comes as other chipmakers pursue similar strategies. Intel announced plans to ship an AI chip later this year using cheaper memory and cooling technology than its California rivals. Intel's new graphics processing unit, codenamed Crescent Island, is being positioned as purpose-built for the upcoming generation of AI agents.

Addressing concerns about AI's impact on employment, Huang dismissed suggestions that the technology would reduce jobs, arguing instead that it would increase demand for software engineers by making workers more productive.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemma 4 12B AI model that runs entirely on 16GB laptops
cards.teaser: Google launched AI Edge Gallery for macOS and introduced Gemma 4 12B, an open source multimodal model designed to run locally on standard laptops.
cards.body:
Google released AI Edge Gallery for macOS, enabling Mac users to run Gemini models locally without internet connectivity. The company also introduced Gemma 4 12B, an open source AI model designed to handle audio and video processing while operating entirely on laptops with 16GB of RAM.

The unified, encoder-free model enables local workflows on standard enterprise laptops, making advanced AI capabilities available without cloud services or specialized hardware. This release reflects Google's broader push to bring AI processing capabilities directly to consumer devices.

cards.headline: NASA ends MAVEN Mars orbiter mission after spacecraft loses control
cards.teaser: NASA declared the end of the MAVEN Mars mission after the orbiter spun out of control and suffered an abrupt demise.
cards.body:
NASA announced the end of its MAVEN Mars mission after the longtime orbiter experienced a sudden failure. The spacecraft spun out of control, leading the agency to declare the mission over after years of studying the Martian atmosphere and environment.

The Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution spacecraft had been orbiting the red planet for an extended period, providing data about Mars' upper atmosphere and climate history. NASA hosted a media call to announce the farewell to the mission, which CBS News described as a long-lasting Mars orbiter that met an abrupt demise. The loss represents the end of a significant NASA planetary science mission.

cards.headline: Nintendo confirms Switch 2 variant with replaceable battery for European Union
cards.teaser: Nintendo will sell a version of the Switch 2 with a user-replaceable battery exclusively in the European Union to comply with regional regulations.
cards.body:
Nintendo has confirmed plans to sell Switch 2 consoles with replaceable batteries in the European Union. The company is implementing this change to comply with new EU regulations set to take effect on February 18th, 2027, which govern electronic device repairability and battery replacement.

The replaceable battery feature will be available specifically for the EU market, with Nintendo registering new device designs with European authorities to meet the regulatory requirements.

cards.headline: Meteor composed of iron exploded over Massachusetts coast
cards.teaser: NASA confirmed that a meteor that broke apart over Cape Cod and the Massachusetts coast was made of iron.
cards.body:
A meteor approximately three feet across entered the atmosphere over New England at 75,000 miles per hour and exploded with the energy of roughly 300 tons of TNT. NASA confirmed the space rock was composed of iron after it broke apart over the Massachusetts coast, causing a loud boom heard by residents.

The explosion occurred over the Boston area and Cape Cod. NBC Boston reported new details about the size and landing location of the meteor fragments. Avi Loeb commented on the meteor explosion, providing analysis of the event that took place on a Saturday afternoon in May 2026. The atmospheric breakup scattered debris over the coastal region.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm infection detected in South Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed a case of flesh-eating screwworm in South Texas, marking the parasite's first breach of the U.S.-Mexico border.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a case of screwworm infection in South Texas, representing the first time the flesh-eating parasite has crossed the U.S.-Mexico border. The detection raises concerns about the spread of the invasive fly species, which lays eggs in open wounds on animals and humans.

Screwworm larvae feed on living tissue, creating serious health risks for livestock and potentially humans. The confirmation of this case marks a significant development in pest control efforts along the southern border, where officials have worked to prevent the northward spread of the parasite. The USDA has previously maintained eradication programs to keep screwworm out of the United States.

cards.headline: Aurora borealis may be visible in eight states Wednesday night
cards.teaser: Geomagnetic storm

hero.headline: Russell Wilson retires from NFL at 37, joins CBS Sports
hero.body:
Veteran quarterback Russell Wilson has retired from professional football at age 37 and will join CBS Sports in a broadcasting role. Wilson confirmed his decision after a career spanning over a decade in the NFL.

Wilson led the Seattle Seahawks to their first Super Bowl championship in 2014, establishing himself as one of the premier quarterbacks of his generation. During his time with Seattle, he became known for his mobility, leadership, and ability to engineer late-game comebacks. He spent the majority of his career with the Seahawks before playing his final seasons with other teams.

The announcement marks the end of a playing career that saw Wilson become one of the most successful quarterbacks in recent NFL history. He departs the league having made multiple Pro Bowl appearances and maintaining a reputation as one of the most consistent performers at his position. His Super Bowl victory in 2014 represented a pinnacle achievement for both Wilson and the Seahawks franchise.

Wilson will transition directly into a media role with CBS Sports, where he will work as a broadcaster. The network finalized a deal with the former quarterback to bring his football expertise to their coverage. His move follows a pattern of high-profile retired players moving into television roles shortly after ending their playing careers.

The retirement removes one of the veteran presences from the quarterback position across the NFL. Wilson posted a video message thanking football as he announced his transition to broadcasting. His departure comes as teams continue their preparations for the upcoming season without one of the familiar faces who defined the position over the past decade.

cards.headline: Knicks take Game 1 of NBA Finals with comeback win over Spurs
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks erased a 14-point third-quarter deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs in the opening game of the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-95 in Game 1 of the NBA Finals, securing victory on the road despite a strong challenge from the defending champion-killers. Jalen Brunson led the way with 30 points as New York kept Victor Wembanyama quiet for stretches throughout the contest.

The win extends the Knicks' remarkable playoff run to 11 consecutive victories. New York now needs just three more wins to claim their first NBA championship since 1973.

cards.headline: FIFA bans reusable water bottles from World Cup stadiums
cards.teaser: Fans will not be allowed to bring reusable water bottles into World Cup stadiums under a late policy change by FIFA citing safety concerns.
cards.body:
FIFA has banned fans from bringing reusable water bottles into World Cup stadiums, citing safety concerns. The governing body reversed its earlier policy that permitted empty, transparent plastic bottles inside venues, implementing the change through an updated stadium code of conduct.

The prohibition extends to other containers including bottles, cups, jars and cans. FIFA said the restriction aims to prevent the risk of injury to players and spectators if items are thrown during matches.

cards.headline: Manchester City dismiss Haaland move after Real Madrid candidate unveils shirt
cards.teaser: Manchester City are considering legal action after a candidate in Real Madrid's presidential election displayed an Erling Haaland shirt on live television.
cards.body:
A Real Madrid presidential candidate, Enrique Riquelme, held up a shirt bearing Erling Haaland's name during a televised appearance, claiming a contract clause would allow him to sign the Manchester City striker if elected. Riquelme also promised that Rodri would join Real Madrid.

Manchester City has dismissed the prospect of Haaland's departure and is considering legal action against Riquelme over the incident. Haaland signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract with City in January 2025.

cards.headline: Lamine Yamal prepares for World Cup as Spain's key player at 18
cards.teaser: At 18 years old, Lamine Yamal has become a central figure in Spain's World Cup squad, though he is quick to dismiss comparisons to Lionel Messi.
cards.body:
I can see that the BBC Sport source is directly about Lamine Yamal and the World Cup, so I'll rewrite the card based on confirmed facts from that source:

Lamine Yamal holds a central position in Spain's World Cup squad at just 18 years old. The young player has attracted significant attention from observers who believe he possesses exceptional potential.

Despite the comparisons being made to Lionel Messi, Yamal himself has been dismissive of such parallels. He remains focused on his role in Spain's World Cup campaign.

cards.headline: Marcelo Bielsa to lead Uruguay at World Cup
cards.teaser: Marcelo Bielsa, the former Leeds United manager known for his extensive video analysis, will guide Uruguay at the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
Marcelo Bielsa will serve as Uruguay's manager at the World Cup. The former Leeds United boss has built a reputation as one of football's most dedicated students of the game, possibly having watched more football than anyone alive today.

Bielsa's meticulous approach includes maintaining extensive video archives of matches. His methods during his time at Leeds included detailed preparation and analysis that became hallmarks of his coaching style.

cards.headline: Chelsea striker Liam Delap scores twice in injury-hit first season
cards.teaser: Liam Delap managed just two goals in 41 games during his first year at Chelsea, with injuries limiting his impact.
cards.body:
A year into his Chelsea career, striker Liam Delap has endured a difficult debut season, managing just two goals across 41 appearances. Injuries played a significant role in limiting his impact on the pitch during the campaign.

The underwhelming return has left questions hanging over Delap's future at the club as he looks to turn things around in the seasons ahead.

hero.headline: Ted Danson Apologizes for 1993 Blackface Performance at Whoopi Goldberg Roast
hero.body:
Ted Danson said he will spend the rest of his life apologizing for wearing blackface during a 1993 roast of Whoopi Goldberg at the New York Friars Club. The actor addressed the incident during an appearance on W. Kamau Bell's podcast, calling his decision arrogant and stupid.

Danson performed the roast while he and Goldberg were in a relationship. The performance drew immediate criticism and controversy at the time. The actor acknowledged the severity of his actions more than three decades later, expressing lasting regret for the choice.

The Cheers and The Good Place star reflected on the incident as a significant error in judgment. Blackface has a deeply racist history in American entertainment, used historically to mock and demean Black people through caricatured performances by white actors. The practice is widely recognized as offensive and harmful.

Danson's comments come during a broader cultural reckoning with past entertainment practices that perpetuated racial stereotypes. Many performers and public figures have faced renewed scrutiny for past actions involving blackface, leading to apologies and in some cases the removal of content from streaming platforms.

The actor's willingness to discuss the incident openly represents an acknowledgment of its ongoing impact. Goldberg and Danson ended their relationship in 1994. Danson has continued working in television, most recently appearing in series including A Man on the Inside and the Fargo television adaptation.

cards.headline: Kathy Hilton Steps Down as West Hollywood Pride Grand Marshal
cards.teaser: The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills star withdrew from the honorary role following community criticism over alleged ties to Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Kathy Hilton announced she will not serve as grand marshal icon for the 2026 West Hollywood Pride Parade. The decision followed pushback from community members over her alleged connections to Donald Trump.

The City of West Hollywood had previously announced Hilton as the grand marshal icon for the parade. The reality television star's withdrawal came after controversy emerged around her political associations. West Hollywood Pride organizers have not announced a replacement for the role.

cards.headline: Bob Harris to Leave BBC Radio 2 After 56 Years
cards.teaser: The veteran broadcaster announced his departure from the station while undergoing cancer treatment.
cards.body:
Bob Harris will step down from BBC Radio 2 after more than five decades on air. The broadcaster described the decision as the hardest he had ever made.

Harris is currently receiving treatment for cancer. His tenure at Radio 2 spans 56 years, making him one of the longest-serving presenters in British radio history. The broadcaster has not announced specific plans for his final broadcast date.

cards.headline: Neon Wins Seventh Consecutive Palme d'Or at Cannes
cards.teaser: The independent distributor's latest win came for Cristian Mungiu's film Fjord, continuing an extraordinary festival run.
cards.body:
Neon secured its seventh consecutive Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival with Cristian Mungiu's "Fjord." Tom Quinn, an executive at the independent distributor, discussed the achievement during a talk at SXSW London, which he attended less than two weeks after the Cannes ceremony.

The win underscores Neon's emergence as a dominant force at the prestigious French festival despite its relative youth in the industry. The distributor will mark its 10th anniversary next year.

cards.headline: Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury Announce Birth of Second Child
cards.teaser: The reality television star shared the news on Instagram with a photo of the family.
cards.body:
Reality TV stars Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury have welcomed their second child. Hague shared the news via Instagram, posting a family photo featuring herself, Fury, their daughter Bambi, and the newborn.

The couple have not yet revealed the baby's name or gender.

cards.headline: Universal Music Signs Jason Zhang in Major Chinese Pop Deal
cards.teaser: The agreement covers recorded music, management, live performances, and international strategy for one of Chinese-language pop's most successful artists.
cards.body:
Universal Music Greater China has signed Jason Zhang, a leading figure in Chinese-language pop music, under a comprehensive agreement. The deal covers recorded music, artist management, live performance strategy, and international expansion, structured through a partnership with Zhang's Planet Culture label.

In a related move, Universal Music Group invested in Solution One, a Thai music distributor. These announcements reflect the company's broader push to strengthen its presence across Asian markets.

cards.headline: Tribeca Festival Opens With Earth, Wind & Fire Documentary
cards.teaser: Robert De Niro used his opening night remarks to criticize Donald Trump as immoral, cruel and corrupt.
cards.body:
The Tribeca Festival opened Wednesday with a documentary about Earth, Wind & Fire. Robert De Niro, the festival's Oscar-winning co-founder, delivered opening remarks that included criticism of Donald Trump, whom he described as immoral, cruel and corrupt without naming him directly.

De Niro used the platform to discuss the festival's mission, which emerged following the September 11 attacks. The festival was established to revitalize the part of New York City affected by the tragedy. De Niro has been increasingly outspoken about his political views in recent years.

hero.headline: Trump intelligence pick triggers Senate rebellion, threatens surveillance powers
hero.body:
President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence has ignited significant backlash from Senate Republicans and created a crisis over the renewal of critical surveillance authorities expiring next week.

Pulte, who currently heads the Federal Housing Finance Agency and is a major Republican donor from a home construction fortune, has no intelligence experience. His selection came days after Tulsi Gabbard left the role. Senior Democrats immediately warned that the appointment could derail a fragile bipartisan agreement to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which permits U.S. intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets operating outside the country without a warrant.

The standoff carries unusual leverage. Republicans need at least eight Democratic votes in the Senate to prevent Section 702 from expiring on June 12. Democratic leaders have made clear that a bipartisan deal could collapse unless Trump reverses the appointment.

Senator Mark Warner, vice-chair of the Senate intelligence committee, criticized Pulte's lack of qualifications. "What qualifications does Mr Pulte bring to the office? He has shown that he is willing to do anything that President Trump wants, legal or otherwise," Warner said during a hearing. In an NPR interview, Warner stated the appointment had upended renewal efforts. "I do not have the confidence I had yesterday," he said, warning that Pulte has "no intelligence background" and "a record of misusing private information."

Senate Majority Leader John Thune offered a notably cool response to his own president's pick, telling reporters that "we don't need a weaponized" national intelligence director and warning that Pulte would face "a lengthy road ahead" if nominated permanently. Thune privately asked Mark Warner whether Democrats could reverse course on the surveillance renewal if Pulte remained in the role.

Former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, who was the only Republican voting against Tulsi Gabbard's confirmation, said on Wednesday that anyone in this role "must have the extensive national security experience required by statute, and no nominee who falls short of this requirement will earn my vote."

Senior Trump administration officials struggled to defend the appointment publicly. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent did not endorse the decision during congressional hearings.

Critics worry Pulte could weaponize the intelligence community against political opponents. He has previously leveled unproven fraud allegations at Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook while at the FHFA, allegations Trump tried to use to remove her from the Fed's board. Cook has denied wrongdoing, and the matter is now before the Supreme Court.

The current Section 702 renewal bill, circulated by Senators Tom Cotton and Chuck Grassley, would extend the program through June 2029 and include new penalties for intelligence abuses and additional FBI search requirements.

cards.headline: Netanyahu tensions with Trump grow over Lebanon military strategy
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces competing pressures from Trump and domestic politics as their military objectives diverge.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's recent disagreement with President Trump over Lebanon strategy has strained their typically close relationship. Trump confirmed he called Netanyahu "crazy" during a heated phone call in which he told the Israeli leader not to bomb Beirut.

Despite their frequent coordination on Iran policy and near-daily conversations, the two leaders have shown diverging priorities. Netanyahu faces pressure from domestic politics while Trump has demonstrated less enthusiasm for military escalation in the region, creating tension in what has otherwise been a closely coordinated partnership on Middle East policy.

cards.headline: National Guard deployment fails to reduce violent crime in Washington
cards.teaser: A new study finds the National Guard's presence in the capital had no effect on violent crime despite deployment since last August.
cards.body:
A new study has found that the National Guard's presence in Washington, D.C. has had no effect on violent crime in the city. The Guard has been deployed since last August as part of a federal task force aimed at combating crime.

Despite these findings, the Guard's deployment is set to expand, with troop numbers doubling in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland secured the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor, advancing to the general election this November. A former Biden administration official, Haaland's victory puts her on track to make history.

If elected, she would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

cards.headline: California governor race sees Hilton and Becerra leading primary results
cards.teaser: Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton lead early returns in the race to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra lead California's gubernatorial primary with nearly 60% of votes counted. Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News host, holds a narrow advantage. Becerra, the former health secretary, trails in second place while billionaire environmental activist Tom Steyer runs third as a progressive Democrat.

California's top-two primary system will advance the two highest vote-getters regardless of party to the general election, where they will compete to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Vote counting is expected to take days or weeks to complete.

cards.headline: Stock market holdings reach record share of American household wealth
cards.teaser: Americans now hold a record 33% of their total wealth in stocks, exposing households to greater market volatility.
cards.body:
Americans have placed a record share of their wealth in the stock market, with stocks now representing 33% of total household sector wealth. The figure includes both directly held stocks and shares held indirectly through mutual funds and exchange-traded funds.

The AI-driven market rally has enriched Americans more than usual due to the elevated stock exposure, but it also leaves households vulnerable to larger losses if the market reverses. The concentration of wealth in equities marks a shift in how American families hold their assets compared to previous decades.

cards.headline: California suburbs lose population in ongoing demographic shift
cards.teaser: Year-over-year population declines in California's suburban areas reveal a deeper demographic transformation across the state.
cards.body:
California's suburban areas are losing population year after year, according to U.S. Census Bureau data. The demographic shift is reshaping America's most populous state in ways that extend beyond the coastal wealthy enclaves typically associated with California population changes.

The continued suburban population decline threatens California's diverse workforce that powers its economy. As families relocate to other states, California risks losing political representation and economic capacity to the destinations where those residents move.
